# Playthrough Strategy

Pre-made strategy for the agent, plus the agent's own notes added as it plays. Every chapter has
its own section below with a **Recruits** table (pre-filled by the human) and an **Agent notes**
area (filled in by the agent). Broad, cross-chapter lessons go under **Broad strategy notes**.

## General Strategy

- Always select "yes" to accept side missions when offered the choice to do so.

## Recruiting Units

In each chapter, there are often units that appear as green units (uncontrollable allies) or red units (enemies). These units can often be recruited by executing the Talk action with a specific player-controlled unit, but there are some more complex conditions that have to be fulfilled in order to recruit some characters. For each chapter, you have been provided a list of the recruitable units that appear and the conditions that need to be fulfilled in order to recruit the character. You should try to recruit units if possible, but it is not a strict requirement.

The chapter sections below cover Lyn mode and Hector mode. Eliwood mode is not covered. Recruits are the same on normal and hard difficulty throughout the entire game, so use the list for your mode regardless of difficulty.

## Promoting Units

Fire Emblem has a mechanic known as promotion, where a unit advances to a stronger class. A unit must be at least level 10 to be promoted, although it can go as high as level 20 before being promoted. It is up to you to decide when it is appropriate to promote a unit.

In virtually all cases, a unit is promoted by using a specific consumable item that matches its class. For example, a knight can use a knight crest to be promoted to a general.

## Broad strategy notes

Cross-chapter lessons the agent adds as it plays. Append below.

- fe7_threat treats YOUR units as walls: a tile marked safe can stop being safe once you move the units that were blocking it. fe7_wait's FALLEN line sometimes misreports mid-battle; confirm with fe7_state. A forecast can commit a menu entry (once it committed a Rescue). A range-2-only enemy (Fenrir) still counters at range 2, so only hit it from adjacent tiles.

### Final Chapter — Light (two parts)

**Objectives:**

Defeat Nergal (boss at (8,2), 75 HP, Def 28 / Res 30). Part 2 (dragon) expected after.

**Recruits:**

None.

**Agent notes:**

s01 attempt notes (in progress):
- Restart starts on turn 1 with 7 units; ATHOS HOLDS Durandal(84)/Armads(85)/Sol Katti(8C). Hector has NO weapon until he trades. Trade turn 1.
- fe7_forecast/fe7_act sometimes fail "action menu could not be located" on certain tiles — try an adjacent tile. A forecast once committed a RESCUE (menu entry 0) by mistake; avoid forecasting from tiles next to allies when unsure.
- Lyn is Lv1 Blade Lord (29 HP, Def 6): her death is game over. Keep her carried (by cls3B #5) or far out of all threat. Attempt 2 lost to this on turn 2.
- Attempt 1 (inherited at turn 11) lost Hector at 7 HP. Turn-1 enemy phase killed units #4 (cls22) and #6 (cls1B) both attempts — keep them back.
- Attempt 3: turn 1 trades + all on '.' tiles = no losses (the 'fallen' readings were tool artifacts). Turn 2 killed the 3 mobile morphs (#13,#14 + chip #16) but Eliwood (Lv2, Res 5) died on enemy turn 2 to the Bolting sage E#5 (range 3-10, moves) + archer. Eliwood/Lyn must be full HP and only in reach of ONE attacker, or carried.
- Attempt 4: T2 killed all 3 mobile morphs (Hector crit, Athos double, Pent double). Athos killed the Bolting sage on T5, but the axe pair (E#8/E#9, cls13) reached 'safe' tiles: fe7_threat counts YOUR units as walls, so tiles behind units you then move are NOT safe. Eliwood died -> game over. Army: Eliwood, Hector, Lyn, Athos, Pent (sage), Hawkeye (berserker), Louise (sniper, bow range 2 only). NO healer.
- Attempt 5 (best so far): T1 Athos to (8,20) and trades Armads to Hector at (7,20); Eliwood/Lyn trade with him; no damage. T2 Athos kills archer #13, Pent+Louise kill #16, Hector+Hawkeye melee #14. T3 carry Lyn. T4 Athos kills Bolting sage from (8,18); axe pair died to Athos counters. T5-6 E#10/E#11 shot from pocket tiles (12,21)/(13,21) across the wall (no counter). Then the NOMAD E#12 (chF8, magic weapon 3D, range 1-2, Move 8, ~29 dmg vs Hector, 38 vs Eliwood) + bishop E#15 arrive from SW on T6: killed Hawkeye (carrying halves Spd -> doubled) and then Hector. POCKET = (12-14,21-22), only entrance (12,23); plug it with ATHOS (takes 14 from the nomad, 0 from the bishop) and keep Hector/lords inside.
- Attempt 6: same opening, all good to T6 (Louise's 0x6C is an ELIXIR - full heal). But Bolting hit Eliwood in the pocket T3 (28), and on T6 the nomad (already at (6,22) at T6 start) hit Hector at (13,19) - a dead end where he could not escape - and killed him T7. Lesson: on T6 KILL the nomad when it arrives: Athos 19 at range 2, Hawkeye melee 16 with 59% crit, Hector 23 finisher. Never park Hector at (13,19). Item probe on Lyn's 0x74 (Hero Crest) weirdly traded her 0x74/0x63 to Athos and spent her turn.
- Attempt 7: T2 Hawkeye missed #14 (cls30, 55 HP, Fenrir range 2 ONLY, AS 25) -> it survived at 34 and DOUBLED Lyn (AS 5) for 44 at (8,25): game over T2. #14 has only 3 melee tiles (10,20),(9,21),(10,22). Lyn/Eliwood get doubled by nearly everything. T2 plan for attempt 8: Louise shoots #14 first (6), then Hawkeye (59% crit), Hector, Eliwood in melee; Athos doubles #13; Pent + Lyn (melee, archers cannot counter) kill #16.
- Attempt 8: Louise attacked #14 from range 2 and was COUNTERED to death (its Fenrir IS range 2 - only melee is safe). Pent vanished from the roster mid-turn (unknown). Lyn died T2 EP. Eliwood's 0x87 = Earth Seal; kills that drop items onto a 5-item unit open a discard menu (Rienfleche).
- PLAN for attempt 9: carry BOTH lords from T1 (Hector carries Eliwood from (9,19); Hawkeye carries Lyn from (7,21); Pent to (6,22), Louise to (6,21)). T2 kill #14 with melee only: Athos tome at range 1 (no counter), Hector, Pent tome at range 1. Archers only scratch tanks.
- Attempt 9 (BEST): plan above worked. T2 Athos 26 + Pent 11 (both point-blank, no counter) + Louise crit killed #14; T3 Pent/Louise finished archers; T4 Athos killed sage from (7,17), axes died on Athos T4EP; T5 Pent+Athos+Louise killed E#10/E#11 from the pocket; T6 lords dropped inside pocket (Eliwood 14,22 / Lyn 13,21), Pent plug (12,23), Athos chips nomad; T7 Athos kills nomad (it sat 2 tiles away), T8 Athos kills bishop. Then MISTAKE: Athos left outside at (8,22) and the HERO E#6 (cls10, chF4, weapon 0x90, ATK ~40, AS ~27, Def18 Res22, melee only) doubled him dead T8EP; army collapsed. Lesson: on T8 focus the Hero: Athos 22 at range 2 (no counter) + Pent 7x2 + Hawkeye melee (59% crit), and keep Athos away from it. Without Athos, Nergal (75 HP, Def 28, Res 30) is unbeatable.
- Attempt 10 (s01, LEFT IN PROGRESS, turn 11): Athos crit #14 and Pent crit #13 on T2, but the sage Bolted Hector twice (47->5; it targets carriers). Athos killed sage T4 and both axes, then sat at 9 HP; Pent and Louise died T5EP to the early-arriving nomad/bishop; Hawkeye crit-killed the nomad T7. Athos fled north to (7,8) and then to (7,14) and died T8EP to E#3/E#4/E#7/E#11; Hawkeye died T9EP. Board now: Eliwood 1 HP, Hector 5 HP carrying Lyn, all in the pocket; enemies stopped advancing (stalemate). The chapter is NOT winnable from here (no Athos, Nergal walled off). The runbook forbids a deliberate restart on attempt >=4, so s01 stopped and is handing this to the human: suggest allowing a Restart Chapter.
- Nergal's throne (8,2) is walled off: (7-9,5-7) read 'Wall', so a path must open by an event (kill all the morphs? a turn count?). Unverified.
- Hard truths: no healer, Hector Res 12 is the sage's favourite target, and Athos dies to any physical double (Hero E#6, axes). Only Athos can hurt Nergal.

The search didn't turn up a source that covers the specific question of stairs being blocked and doors opening on turns in the Blazing Sword final chapter, so I can only partly answer it.

- **Turn-based room openings:** A Fire Emblem Heroes guide to "Final Chapter: Light Part I" describes the battle as a sequence of rooms that open on set turns, each with enemies to defeat. The southeast room opens on turn 1, and other rooms open on turns 2 through 6, each with specific enemies such as Uhai, Kenneth, Brendan, Darin, and Ursula. The guide is for the Heroes version, so its map details may not match the original game exactly.
- **Doors:** A FunTrivia quiz notes that Unlock can't be used because there are no manually locked doors in the Final Chapter. This suggests the doors are opened by game events rather than by the player's keys.
- **Morphs:** The same quiz says you fight Brendan Reed at the end as a Morph, which is one of the few morph references I found.
- **Stairs:** None of the results mention stairs being blocked. A Blazing Sword let's play archive describes the final map as a moderately sized puzzle-y kind of level, and says the Gate is open, ready for Nergal to call dragons through it, but it doesn't explain the stair mechanics.

The Fire Emblem Wiki's Blazing Sword pages and the Sacred Stones question page were not useful for this detail. A more targeted search, such as the Blazing Sword "Final Chapter: Light" walkthrough on a dedicated guide site, would probably settle the stairs and turn-trigger question.

The search points to Fire Emblem: The Blazing Blade (the Blazing Sword localization) and its chapter "Light," which is the first part of the Final Chapter. Nergal is the chapter's boss, not a separate path.

- **Sealed rooms:** Nergal is locked in a room at the top of the map that opens only after the other enemies are cleared. Those rooms contain Nergal's special morphs, which are upgraded versions of previous bosses, with the exception of Brendan, who was never fought earlier. Four of the six rooms also contain other strong but generic morphs.
- **Opening doors:** The walkthroughs say the rooms can be opened with a Thief or door keys, except Nergal's room. One turn after Nergal's door is opened, three Generals appear below and two Druids appear above Nergal.
- **Reinforcements:** Enemies arrive by turn, with Kenneth on turn 2, Brendan on turn 3, Darin on turn 4, Ursula and Jerme on turn 5, and Lloyd and Linus on turn 6 (per the turn-by-turn reinforcement list).
- **Athos:** Athos joins at the start of the chapter. One walkthrough notes that Athos attacking with Aureola can remove almost half of Nergal's HP, and advises waiting for Nergal's counterattack before attacking again.
- **Strategy:** One guide advises that you should take "A" rank weapons or higher, since the others will be largely useless.
- **Part 2:** After Nergal is defeated, the true final enemy appears. Wiki sources list the Part 2 boss as a Dragon.

Sources disagree slightly on the room counts and the exact reinforcement details, so check the linked guides if precision matters.

content.text:
I did not win the Final Chapter. I played attempts 11 through 18, and every one ended in game over. The game is now back at the title screen after attempt 18's game over.

**What happened**
- I picked up attempt 10 at turn 11, where it could no longer be won (Athos dead, Eliwood at 1 HP). It ended in game over on my first move. After that the runbook allowed restarting, which I did seven times.
- The best runs killed the sage, both warriors, the nomad, the bishop and the generals. Every run still collapsed once Athos was caught by two heavy hitters (the warriors, or the Hero and paladin when their room opens on turn 6). Without Athos nobody can damage Nergal.
- One thing from my own play is worth knowing: a "turtle" setup at the pocket at (12–14, 21–24) does keep the lords safe. It only fails if Athos ends up stranded outside it or the sage is left alive.

**Why the throne always looked walled off**
I looked up how this chapter works in the real game ([Fire Emblem WoD guide](https://www.fireemblemwod.com/fe7/guiafe7/ENG_capitulo-finalE.htm), [Fire Emblem Wiki](https://fireemblemwiki.org/wiki/Light_(part_1))):
- The staircase to Nergal only opens after every other enemy is dead. That includes the stationary pair in the northwest room and the two casters beside the throne.
- One turn after it opens, three generals and two druids appear as reinforcements.
- Athos should fight Nergal with Aureola, which takes nearly half his HP.

All of that, plus a turn-by-turn record of each attempt and the specific rules I worked out, is in the chapter's notes in `CURRENT_RUN_STRATEGY.md`. The next session should restart the chapter from the title menu.

**Recommendation**
With no healer, one damage dealer, and every enemy on the map needing to die before Nergal is even reachable, I don't think this save can realistically be won as it stands. It probably needs your call: a different save, more units, or accepting it as the end of the run.

**State files**
- `run_state.json`: `attempts` is left at 18 so the next session's +1 counts its restart correctly.
- No chapter was won, so `completed`, `dead` and `unrecruited` are unchanged, and no save state was made.
- I'm deliberately ending without the `PLAYTHROUGH_RESULT=WON` line, so the loop will treat this session as a crash and start a new one on the same chapter.
